memories.memory_text: I saw the Terry Hale bang his gavel and call out in a ritual tone that the herd was now called to the prairie, then command 'Antlers... up!'—and all of us raised our antlers together as the meeting officially began.

grounded_facts: Logan Dalton objects publicly to Evan Nolan's preferential description of Harper Arden, demanding equal recognition.
Logan Dalton objects to Evan Nolan's phrasing that favors Harper Arden over other candidates.
memories.memory_text: I was standing there when Logan Dalton objected, asking why I was introduced as 'good old Harper Arden' while he and the others were just called 'some other guys'—it was clear he felt I was being favored.

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan unveils a hidden campaign poster supporting Harper Arden.
memories.memory_text: I saw Evan Nolan pull a rolled-up tapestry from behind a plant and hang it on the wall—it was a big 'VOTE FOR Harper Arden' poster.

grounded_facts: A formal gathering of the Water Buffalo Silverline Records members to conduct Silverline Records business and hear candidate speeches.
memories.memory_text: I realized this gathering was a formal Water Buffalo Silverline Records meeting where we'd conduct business and hear speeches, especially since I was heading up to the podium with my notes after Evan Nolan handed them to me.

grounded_facts: The Terry Hale hands Harper Arden the ceremonial hoof and antler before his speech.
memories.memory_text: I remember the Terry Hale handing me the ceremonial hoof and antler just before my speech, like a Pharaoh's badges of office.

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan secretly provides Harper Arden with speech notes to help him succeed in his candidacy speech.
Evan Nolan hands Harper Arden a hidden document containing crib notes for his speech.
memories.memory_text: I remember Evan Nolan catching up to me and handing me a document, which I took and later unrolled at the podium—it had crib notes to help me with my speech.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden gives a speech for the Terry Hale position, using Evan Nolan's notes and receiving applause.
memories.memory_text: I gave my speech for the Terry Hale position using Evan Nolan's notes, and when I finished, I got applause from the crowd.

grounded_facts: A lizard used as a bottle opener is knocked under the counter, where an impact straightens its overbite, leading it to leave the Silverline Records happily.
memories.memory_text: I used that lizard to open a few beers, then tossed it under the counter where it bounced off the shelf; later, I noticed it had straightened its overbite from the impact and happily walked out with a hat and coat.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden raises a drink in honor of the Silverline Records, prompting a reciprocal toast from Evan Nolan.
memories.memory_text: I raised my drink and said, 'Here's to the greatest bunch of lifelong Buffaloes a guy could dream of leading,' and then Evan Nolan toasted me right back, calling me the next Terry Hale.

grounded_facts: A social gathering of Silverline Records members at the recreation area, featuring bowling, drinks, and camaraderie.
memories.memory_text: I was at the Silverline Records with the guys, bowling strikes and sharing drinks, feeling the camaraderie as my friends raised a toast to me becoming the next Terry Hale.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden announces he has become Assistant Junior Vice President of Public Relations at Lakeside Medical Center, showing a stone business card as proof.
memories.memory_text: I announced to the Silverline Records that I've been promoted to Assistant Junior Vice President of Public Relations at Lakeside Medical Center, and I showed them my stone business card to prove it.

grounded_facts: Reese Hawthorne doubts the authenticity of Harper Arden's business card and attempts to prove it fake by biting it, resulting in a cracked tooth.
memories.memory_text: I saw Reese Hawthorne doubt my business card was real, and he tried to prove it was fake by biting it—then winced when his tooth cracked.

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan questions Harper Arden's assertion of acting 'single-handedly' in securing the promotion, reminding him of his own contribution.
memories.memory_text: I remember Evan Nolan reacting when I said I did it single-handedly, and he called out to me, reminding me that he had a big part in it too, saying he distinctly remembered at least four hands involved, two of them his.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden privately explains to Evan Nolan that while he will be the public face of their success, Evan Nolan is the 'brains behind the operation' and will serve as the silent partner.
memories.memory_text: I pulled Evan Nolan aside into the corridor near the trophy case and explained that while I'd be the public face of our success, he'd be the silent partner—the brains behind the operation—while I was the brains in front, running things out in the open, and I shook his hand confidently to seal it.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden departs for his first day at the leather watch, receiving a symbolic gift from Jonah Adler.
memories.memory_text: I was about to leave for my first day at the leather watch when Jonah Adler called me back, saying something was wrong with my lunch—I opened my pail and found it empty, but then she surprised me with a new briefcase, embossed with 'F.F', and I saw it had a lock, buckles, and even a strap, and when I opened it, there was a big drumstick and ribs inside, and I felt touched by her gesture.

grounded_facts: Jonah Adler surprises Harper Arden with a new briefcase filled with food, replacing his empty lunch pail.
memories.memory_text: I was surprised when I opened my lunch pail and found it empty, but then Jonah Adler handed me a brand new briefcase with 'F.F' on it, and when I opened it, there was a big drumstick and some ribs inside.

grounded_facts: Jonah Adler uses financial jargon humorously to warn Harper Arden about workplace dangers.
memories.memory_text: I remember Jonah Adler kissed me and told me to watch out for those 'hostile takeovers' as a joke before I left for work.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden and Evan Nolan use exaggerated formalities to greet each other before work.
memories.memory_text: I greeted Evan Nolan with a mock-formal 'Ah, Mister Evan Nolan, I presume? Of the the leather watch Rubbles?' to mark the start of our workday together.

grounded_facts: The the leather watch program begins implementation at the Harborview Station, involving resource delivery and personnel restructuring.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Shawn Ellison looking out the window and signing a form, and later heard him talking about the the leather watch program bringing changes to Harborview Station, including shifting Logan Dalton’s role to stir up trouble among the workers, so I figured the program must be starting up with some behind-the-scenes restructuring and resource moves.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden and Evan Nolan arrive at Harborview Station lot in Harper Arden's car, evading Skyler Sterling's patrol car by ducking down.
memories.memory_text: I drove my car into Harborview Station lot and made a quick turn, then I ducked down with Evan Nolan to avoid being seen by Skyler Sterling's patrol car.

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan compliments Harper Arden's driving as being more exciting than a theme park ride.
memories.memory_text: Evan Nolan told me that driving with me is better than an 'E' ticket at Magerock Mountain.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden and Evan Nolan learn that the employee basketball court has been replaced by the the leather watch assembly line.
memories.memory_text: I was told the employee basketball court had been replaced by the the leather watch assembly line.

grounded_facts: Shawn Ellison directs Harper Arden and Evan Nolan to their offices and tells them to later attend the formula review.
memories.memory_text: Shawn Ellison told me and Evan Nolan to settle into our new offices and then attend the formula review at the assembly line.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden and Evan Nolan are led to their new offices in a wood-sided trailer with poor conditions.
memories.memory_text: I saw that my new office was in a wood-sided trailer with a tiny desk, a flimsy divider, and a window looking out over Harborview Station scrap heap.

grounded_facts: The the leather watch assembly line successfully produces replicas of stone items using foam and molds.
memories.memory_text: I saw the the leather watch assembly line start up, and I was there when Evan Nolan pulled the rope to pour the foam into the mold, making the first stone-like product.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden and Evan Nolan are introduced to the the leather watch assembly line and participate in its first production run.
memories.memory_text: I was introduced to the the leather watch assembly line and took part in its first production run, watching the finished sofas get stacked easily by the workers.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden and Evan Nolan celebrate their new executive positions with high-fives and handshakes.
memories.memory_text: I celebrated my new executive position with Evan Nolan, and we shared high-fives and a handshake to mark the moment together.

grounded_facts: Morgan Foster announces that 22 laborers will be laid off and replaced by children from Bedrock Technical Junior High.
memories.memory_text: I heard Morgan Foster announce that 22 laborers would be laid off and replaced by children from Bedrock Technical Junior High.

grounded_facts: Morgan Foster addresses the workers to celebrate the first the leather watch products and announces layoffs.
memories.memory_text: I saw Morgan Foster come out to the balcony and announce that the first the leather watch products were a success, and then he said they'd be hiring children to replace dozens of workers, including 22 who were being laid off.

grounded_facts: Workers express anger and blame Harper Arden for their layoffs.
memories.memory_text: I saw the workers turn angry and heard them blame me, asking 'Thanks to Harper Arden?' and calling out 'Jonah Adler! What kinda shop steward are you?'

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan prompts Harper Arden to take responsibility for the workers' situation.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Evan Nolan prompts Harper Arden to take responsibility for the workers' situation.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden realizes he must take action in response to the workers' anger and layoffs.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Harper Arden realizes he must take action in response to the workers' anger and layoffs.

grounded_facts: Morgan Foster demonstrates his power to fire anyone at will, using finger snaps and humor to underscore control.
memories.memory_text: I barged into Morgan Foster's office to speak up about the long-time workers, and when I challenged him about laying anyone off just like that with a snap of his fingers, he laughed and said he could fire Shawn Ellison or even me if he wanted to — and I realized he wasn't just joking.

grounded_facts: Morgan Foster jokes about firing Harper Arden, initially perceived as humor but later revealed as a veiled threat.
memories.memory_text: I heard Morgan Foster say he could fire me, and at first I laughed because I thought he was joking, but then I stopped laughing when I realized he might actually mean it.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden attempts to advocate for long-term workers but is overruled and socially pressured into silence.
memories.memory_text: I tried to speak up for the guys who'd been at Harborview Station for years, but I could feel Shawn Ellison watching me, and when Morgan Foster made it clear I had no choice, I realized I couldn't risk my job—I had to stay silent.

grounded_facts: Morgan Foster shifts from joking to serious tone, implying Harper Arden's job is at risk unless he backs down.
Morgan Foster tells Harper Arden to leave if he wants to keep his job, using implied threat.
memories.memory_text: I remember Morgan Foster shifting from joking to serious, telling me he could fire me and that he had a bad feeling about me—if I wanted that to go away, I should just leave. I swallowed hard, looked at Shawn Ellison, and walked out quietly, knowing my job depended on it.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden confronts Morgan Foster about laying off long-term workers, leading to a tense exchange in the office.
memories.memory_text: I confronted Morgan Foster about laying off the long-term workers because I knew they deserved better, but when he told me to walk out and forget it, I just swallowed and left quietly.

grounded_facts: Workers assemble in Harborview Station yard awaiting the result of Harper Arden's negotiation with management.
memories.memory_text: I remember all the workers watching me as I came out, waiting to hear what happened with management.

grounded_facts: Workers collectively ask Harper Arden about the outcome of his negotiation with management.
memories.memory_text: I heard the workers asking me, 'Right, Harper Arden...? Harper Arden...?' while they waited for news about the raise.

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan voices worry after Harper Arden responds incoherently and begins to stagger.
memories.memory_text: I heard Evan Nolan say my name, 'Harper Arden?', when I started to stagger, sounding worried.

grounded_facts: The workers realize that Harper Arden did not succeed in securing a raise, as he retreats silently and emotionally into his locker.
memories.memory_text: I retreated into my locker and broke down, and I knew the workers realized I hadn't gotten the raise.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden discovers his posters and childhood photo have been defaced with horns and the name 'Harper Arden Finkstone'.
memories.memory_text: I saw that my posters and childhood photo had been changed to say 'Harper Arden Finkstone' and someone had drawn horns and a beard on my face, making me look like a demon or a joke.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden physically maneuvers Evan Nolan into the spotlight and demands he tell 'the true story' of the leather watch to save his reputation.
memories.memory_text: I grabbed Evan Nolan and pushed him center stage because I needed him to tell the others the true story about the leather watch and clear my name.

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan attempts to support Harper Arden by recounting the the leather watch incident but misremembers it comically, undermining Harper Arden instead.
memories.memory_text: I watched as Evan Nolan tried to help me by recounting the the leather watch incident, but he got it all wrong and made things worse, ending with that stupid wink that made me groan.

grounded_facts: After the vote, Evan Nolan tries to comfort Harper Arden by saying he supported him, but Harper Arden responds with anger and blame.
memories.memory_text: I grabbed Evan Nolan and pushed him center stage, desperate for him to tell the others the true story behind the leather watch, but when he just winked and joked about it, I felt crushed—and when he said he voted for me, I snapped and told him it didn't matter after he'd ruined everything.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden loses the Buffaloes Silverline Records election to Logan Dalton after being isolated and mocked by the members.
memories.memory_text: I lost the election to Logan Dalton after the Silverline Records turned on me—I could hear them snickering, and when I called out that it was rigged, no one stood with me while Logan Dalton took the title right in front of my face.

grounded_facts: A formal gathering of the Buffalo Silverline Records to elect a new Exalted Terry Hale, which turns into a political reckoning over workplace layoffs.
memories.memory_text: I was at the Buffalo Silverline Records election meeting where they installed Logan Dalton as the new Exalted Terry Hale, and when the new leader started talking about how most of us wouldn't be able to make our cave payments next month, everyone suddenly turned and looked at me before looking away.

grounded_facts: After electing Logan Dalton, the Silverline Records decides to attack Harborview Station and destroy the assembly line in protest.
memories.memory_text: I was there when Logan Dalton gave his speech after winning the election, and I heard him tell the Silverline Records it was time to stand up and be a man — then he rallied everyone to go destroy the assembly line at the Harborview Station.

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan alerts Harper Arden that the Buffaloes, led by Logan Dalton, are heading to Harborview Station to destroy the assembly line.
memories.memory_text: I remember Evan Nolan rushing up to me, shouting that the Buffaloes were heading into big trouble — Logan Dalton had stirred everyone up and they were on their way to Harborview Station to wreck the assembly line.

grounded_facts: Logan Dalton encourages the mob to destroy property and assert dominance over management.
memories.memory_text: I heard Logan Dalton shout to start with Morgan Foster's golf trophies and work up to the assembly line, encouraging the mob to destroy property.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden questions how the situation escalated so far.
memories.memory_text: I couldn't believe how out of hand things had gotten, and I remember asking myself how everything escalated so far.

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan wishes things were back to the way they were before they became executives.
memories.memory_text: Evan Nolan told me he wished things were back the way they were before we became executives, and I heard him say it clearly.

grounded_facts: Skyler Sterling uses a megaphone to order Harper Arden to pull over.
memories.memory_text: I heard Skyler Sterling shout through a megaphone, ordering me to pull over, and I saw him in the patrol car behind me.

grounded_facts: A whale emerges from the broken fire hydrant, speaking and threatening legal action.
The whale speaks to announce intent to sue Skyler Sterling and Terry Carver for damages.
memories.memory_text: I saw a whale burst out of the broken fire hydrant, and I heard it say, 'I'm gonna sue you for everything you got'—I turned to Evan Nolan and asked if he saw that too.

grounded_facts: The Riley Calloway is revealed to have been attempting to break into the Morgan Foster Company safe, fleeing upon being disturbed.
memories.memory_text: I realized the Riley Calloway had been trying to break into the Morgan Foster safe after seeing it drop tools, grab them in a panic, and vanish right as I noticed—something wasn't right about that scene.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden briefly perceives the Riley Calloway near the safe but then doubts his eyes.
memories.memory_text: I saw something near the safe—jumped up, startled—and I called out to Barn, but by the time I looked again, it was gone. I could've sworn it was the Riley Calloway, but now I'm doubting myself.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden and Evan Nolan lose control of their car and crash into the main Harborview Station building, creating a hole in the wall.
memories.memory_text: I was driving with Evan Nolan when we lost control and crashed into the main Harborview Station building, punching a hole through the wall.

grounded_facts: Logan Dalton leads an angry mob over the gate of Harborview Station, initiating a raid on Morgan Foster's facility.
A mob of angry workers, led by Logan Dalton, attacks the Harborview Station and plant in protest.
memories.memory_text: I saw Logan Dalton lead a mob of angry workers over Harborview Station gate and rush into Morgan Foster's plant, attacking the facility.

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan stops Reese Hawthorne from smashing a light fixture by pulling it up, initiating their chase in the rafters.
memories.memory_text: I saw Evan Nolan drop down from the rafters and pull up the light fixture just in time to stop Reese Hawthorne from smashing it, which started their chase.

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan teases Reese Hawthorne after dodging his swing and causing him to fall.
memories.memory_text: I heard Evan Nolan tease Reese Hawthorne with a laugh after dodging his swing and making him fall, yelling something like 'Stee-rike one!' as the chase began.

grounded_facts: Logan Dalton and Reese Hawthorne lead workers in destroying the assembly line infrastructure.
memories.memory_text: I saw Logan Dalton and Reese Hawthorne leading the workers to destroy the assembly line, smashing light fixtures and snapping support beams to bring down the infrastructure.

grounded_facts: Logan Dalton and Reese Hawthorne direct rampaging workers up to the assembly line catwalk to escalate sabotage.
memories.memory_text: I figured Logan Dalton and Reese Hawthorne were trying to make things worse by sending the workers up to the catwalk, though I didn't see them give the order directly.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden reveals himself as the counterweight on a beam Logan Dalton is trying to break, leading to a physical struggle.
memories.memory_text: I revealed myself as the counterweight on the beam where Logan Dalton was trying to break through, and when he realized I was there, I inched down and jumped off—my weight had already boinged the beam down on his head. Then I backpedaled away from him on the assembly line, trying to stay ahead of his chase.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden draws imaginary lines to trick Logan Dalton into falling off the edge.
memories.memory_text: I dared Logan Dalton to cross the line I drew, and I saw him fall for it—he stepped right over and almost went off the edge.

grounded_facts: The impact of Harper Arden landing in the mold triggers the assembly line to start producing Fibre Harper Arden statues.
memories.memory_text: I landed hard in the clay mold, and the impact set off the assembly line—when the goatasauruses rammed the mold, it spat out a Fibre statue of me.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden and Logan Dalton fall after Logan Dalton grabs Harper Arden's clothing; Harper Arden lands in a clay mold, triggering automated production.
memories.memory_text: I fell after Logan Dalton grabbed my clothes, and I landed hard in a clay mold—I could feel it close around me, and then the machine started moving me like I was one of those Fibre statues.

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan and Reese Hawthorne engage in a physical chase and fight in the rafters above the assembly line.
memories.memory_text: I watched Evan Nolan and Reese Hawthorne chasing each other through the rafters, dodging swings and smashing windows until Evan Nolan got hit and the fight moved on.

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan uses a rubber stamp to mark Reese Hawthorne's rear as 'REJECT' during their fight, leading to Reese Hawthorne's capture.
memories.memory_text: I saw Evan Nolan grab a rubber stamp and use it to mark Reese Hawthorne's rear as 'REJECT' during their fight, which led to Reese Hawthorne being captured.

grounded_facts: Reese Hawthorne threatens to smash Evan Nolan's head after being stamped 'REJECT'.
memories.memory_text: I heard Reese Hawthorne threaten to smash Evan Nolan's head after being stamped with 'REJECT'.

grounded_facts: The alligator crane carries Reese Hawthorne and drops him into a bin labeled REJECTS, removing him from the conflict.
memories.memory_text: I saw the alligator crane grab Reese Hawthorne by the seat of his pants and swing him over to a big bin marked REJECTS before dropping him in with a howl.

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan jumps into the Fibrefoam chute to intercept Logan Dalton before he attacks the immobilized Harper Arden.
memories.memory_text: I was immobilized and about to be attacked by Logan Dalton when I saw Evan Nolan jump into the Fibrefoam chute and slide down, slamming into both of us and knocking us over.

grounded_facts: Skyler Sterling declares everyone under arrest upon arrival.
memories.memory_text: I heard Skyler Sterling shout that we were all under arrest just as everything went chaotic.

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan intercepts Logan Dalton's attack on the immobilized Harper Arden, resulting in a collision that knocks over the arriving police.
memories.memory_text: I was knocked down and couldn't move when Logan Dalton came at me, but Evan Nolan jumped in and slammed into both of us, sending us rolling across the floor.

grounded_facts: The assembly line produces multiple Fibre statues of Harper Arden, confusing Logan Dalton and concealing the real Harper Arden.
memories.memory_text: I landed in the clay mold and got rammed by the goatasauruses, then got flung onto the conveyor belt where they made Fibre statues of me—I saw one knock me down and I couldn't move when the clay and Fibre hardened all over me, and even though I was stuck, I managed to poke my real head out at the end.

grounded_facts: After being dragged out, Harper Arden's clay-encased head detaches, revealing his real head emerging from the statue.
memories.memory_text: I felt the clay and Fibre all over me solidify, trapping me, and when I was dragged out, my real head slowly emerged from the casing as the clay head detached.

grounded_facts: Skyler Sterling and the police arrive to arrest the participants, but are initially knocked over before regaining control.
memories.memory_text: I saw Skyler Sterling and the police arrive to arrest everyone, but we crashed into them and knocked them over before they finally got us under control and dragged us out.

grounded_facts: Drew Colter asks Evan Nolan to explain the behavior of the men involved in the incident.
memories.memory_text: I overheard Drew Colter asking Evan Nolan what came over us boys at the Silverline Records meeting.

grounded_facts: One of the exiting buffalo verbally threatens Harper Arden as he leaves.
memories.memory_text: I heard one of the buffalo say 'Jonah Adler, you're dead meat' as he was leaving, clearly threatening me.

grounded_facts: Jonah Adler attempts to get Harper Arden to confess or explain what happened at the Silverline Records meeting.
memories.memory_text: Jonah Adler asked me if there was something I wanted to tell her about the Silverline Records meeting.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden refuses to discuss the Silverline Records meeting incident with Jonah Adler, showing emotional withdrawal.
memories.memory_text: I told Jonah Adler I didn't want to talk about the Silverline Records meeting and said I didn't care about those jerks with furs on their heads, because I'm more of a country club guy.

grounded_facts: Shawn Ellison offers Harper Arden a cigar using a bizarre lizard-based cutter, establishing a tone of performative sophistication.
memories.memory_text: I remember Shawn Ellison offering me a cigar with this strange lizard-based cutter, making it feel like I was stepping into a world of status and style.

grounded_facts: When challenged by Shawn Ellison about Evan Nolan's role, Harper Arden downplays his own involvement and hesitates in asserting his contribution.
memories.memory_text: I hesitated when Shawn Ellison asked about Evan Nolan's role, and I found myself downplaying my own part, stumbling over how to describe it without sounding too important.

grounded_facts: Shawn Ellison frames Harper Arden's continued support of Evan Nolan as a hindrance to his own success, urging him to focus on his duties.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Shawn Ellison that keeping up my support for Evan Nolan would hold me back, and that I should focus on my own duties instead.

grounded_facts: Shawn Ellison implies that Harper Arden and Evan Nolan's skepticism about Morgan Foster's leadership is disrespectful, testing Harper Arden's allegiance.
memories.memory_text: I remember Shawn Ellison confronting me, implying that my skepticism with Evan Nolan about Morgan Foster's leadership was a slap in the face to our founder and employer—he really made me feel the weight of that, questioning whether I’d keep covering for Evan Nolan or focus on my own duties.

grounded_facts: A private meeting between Shawn Ellison and Harper Arden in Shawn Ellison's office, where Harper Arden is evaluated and offered a promotional opportunity.
memories.memory_text: I was in Shawn Ellison's office, and he walked me in personally before telling me I was cut out for the big time, and then Owen Arden showed up and said they were going to put me on their program—I realized this was a real chance for something bigger.

grounded_facts: Shawn Ellison reveals a plan to promote Harper Arden on television as a reward for his role in making the leather watch famous, contingent on distancing from Evan Nolan.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Shawn Ellison that I’d be promoted on television as a reward for my role in making the leather watch famous, but only if I distanced myself from Evan Nolan.

grounded_facts: Shawn Ellison introduces Harper Arden to Owen Arden, a television personality who will feature Harper Arden on his show, contingent on Harper Arden distancing from Evan Nolan.
memories.memory_text: I saw Shawn Ellison open the door and was surprised to see Owen Arden, who greeted me and said I’d be on his show as long as I let go of Evan Nolan.

grounded_facts: Owen Arden observes the Evan Nolan yard and deems it unsuitable for the show's image due to barbecues and tricycles.
Owen Arden visually inspects the Evan Nolan yard and dismisses it as incompatible with the show's image.
memories.memory_text: I heard Owen Arden say the Evan Nolan yard with its barbecues and tricycles didn't fit the show's image, and he dismissed it after looking at it.

grounded_facts: A live television broadcast crew films at the Jonah Adler house, transforming the setting into a staged production site.
memories.memory_text: I saw the live television crew arrive at my house, setting up trucks and lights, turning everything into a production site.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden conceals his own working-class yard items after realizing they resemble the rejected Evan Nolan yard elements.
memories.memory_text: I think I realized in that moment that my yard items were too much like Evan Nolan's—what we both considered undesirable—so I figured covering them up was the best way to keep things looking proper for the broadcast.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden notices his own barbecue and tricycles resemble the 'undesirable' items and quickly covers them.
memories.memory_text: I noticed my own barbecue and tricycles looked just like the stuff we didn't want showing up on camera, so I quickly tossed a tarp over them and moved a potted plant to hide them better.

grounded_facts: Crew members move potted plants and nail boards over the fence to block the view of the Evan Nolan yard.
memories.memory_text: I suggested moving the potted plants to block the view, and I saw the crew nail up boards and place the plants to cover the Evan Nolan yard.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden repeatedly interrupts the broadcast to upgrade how his name is presented, culminating in 'Harper Arden'.
memories.memory_text: I kept interrupting the broadcast to make sure they used a more prestigious version of my name, and I even carved 'Harper Arden' into a stone cue card to show them how I wanted to be introduced.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden uses the broadcast to attribute the success of the leather watch to Morgan Foster.
On camera, Harper Arden publicly credits Morgan Foster rather than his friends or family for the invention of the leather watch.
memories.memory_text: I used the broadcast to give full credit for the leather watch's success to Morgan Foster, speaking publicly about his inspiration and support as my close friend and associate, without mentioning my friends or family.

grounded_facts: A public ceremony at Harborview Plaza to inaugurate the Harborview District and Harborview Heights, promoted as a grand event by Lakeside Medical Center.
memories.memory_text: I saw the big event at Harborview Plaza with Mr. and Morgan Foster arriving in a limousine, and Emery Cavendish was excited about cutting in line.

grounded_facts: Jonah Adler criticizes Harper Arden for treating Drew Colter and Evan Nolan poorly due to his pursuit of social status.
memories.memory_text: I remember Jonah Adler coming over to me, concerned, and telling me that I was treating Drew Colter and Evan Nolan horribly — she said I was turning my back on the things that really count just because of a little money.

grounded_facts: The ribbon-cutting ceremony at Harborview Plaza is moved forward by an hour, prompting the end of the Jonah Adler party.
memories.memory_text: I was told the ribbon-cutting ceremony got moved up by an hour, which is why the party had to end early.

grounded_facts: The party at the Jonah Adler house disbands as guests and crew leave for Harborview Plaza.
memories.memory_text: I noticed my audience had suddenly evaporated and saw everyone heading to their cars, with the TV crew packing up, so I realized the party at my house was disbanding as people left for Harborview Plaza.

grounded_facts: A social gathering hosted by Harper Arden and Jonah Adler, intended to impress guests but ultimately failing.
memories.memory_text: I hosted a party at my house and tried to keep everyone entertained, but I noticed people were leaving and I told Jonah Adler they were just party hopping before coming back.

grounded_facts: Drew Colter decides to join Jonah Adler in going to the Harborview Plaza party, affirming their friendship.
Jonah Adler decides to go to the Harborview Plaza party, and Drew Colter chooses to join her, leaving their husbands behind.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jonah Adler and Drew Colter decide to go to the Harborview Plaza party together, leaving me and Evan Nolan behind, and I heard Drew Colter say, 'Jonah Adler, wait. I'm going with you,' and then whisper something about giving the boys some space.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden offers a canape to Finley Reeves, who rejects it and spits it out.
memories.memory_text: I offered Finley Reeves a canape, and I saw him taste it, make a face, and spit it out before running away.

grounded_facts: The immediate aftermath of Harper Arden's failed campaign party, where emotional reckoning occurs.
memories.memory_text: I sat there alone in the mess of what was left of the party, feeling completely defeated, and when Finley Reeves came over to nuzzle me, I thought maybe I wasn't totally alone—then I looked down at my blazer, at that 'FVF' patch, and I just ripped it off in anger.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden smashes the lawn chair and the wall between his and Evan Nolan's property in a fit of anger after the party ends.
memories.memory_text: I grabbed a lawn chair and started smashing it against the wall between my yard and Evan Nolan's, I didn't care anymore—I just needed to let it out, and I kept going until the wall cracked and pieces were flying everywhere.

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan emerges from the ruins of the destroyed wall, revealing he has returned despite Harper Arden's earlier betrayal.
memories.memory_text: I saw the figure standing in the ruins of the wall, sneezing and brushing off dirt, and when I realized it was Evan Nolan, I couldn't believe he was really there after everything.

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan helps Harper Arden articulate his guilt by humorously listing insults.
Harper Arden acknowledges his selfish and hurtful behavior toward Evan Nolan during the party campaign.
memories.memory_text: I started to tell Evan Nolan how sorry I was for being such a jerk, and when I struggled to find the words, he helped me by listing all the names he could call me—creep, fool, slimeball, louse, jackass, even 'stuck-up blimpasaurus'—and in the end, I asked if he could ever forgive me, and he said yes.

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan accepts Harper Arden's apology with humor and warmth, restoring their friendship.
Harper Arden initiates a heartfelt hug after Evan Nolan forgives him.
memories.memory_text: I apologized to Evan Nolan, feeling like such a jerk, and when he smiled and said he'd had lots of practice forgiving me, I just couldn't hold it in anymore—I hugged him tight, and we both got a little teary.

grounded_facts: Finley Reeves rejects Harper Arden's offering and leaves with Drew Colter's family, symbolizing Harper Arden's social isolation.
memories.memory_text: I think Finley Reeves rejected me and left with Drew Colter's family, which makes me wonder if I'm really alone now.

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan retrieves an old footlocker containing their vintage cheerleading costumes, which they then put on.
memories.memory_text: I saw Evan Nolan pull out our old footlocker, and I tossed him his sweater before squeezing into my mascot uniform again, struggling to zip it up but managing in the end.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden and Evan Nolan reminisce about their time at Bedrock High, reflecting on past camaraderie and simpler times.
memories.memory_text: I sang our old school cheer with Evan Nolan, laughing about the good old days at Bedrock High, remembering how we boosted team spirit as cheerleaders—me in that goofy mascot costume—and how simple life felt back then with no real worries.

grounded_facts: An upcoming social gathering hosted by Morgan Foster that Harper Arden and Evan Nolan were expected to attend.
memories.memory_text: I was reminded by Evan Nolan that we were expected at Morgan Foster's party, which brought us back from our trip down memory lane.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden expresses bitterness toward Morgan Foster and his associates, realizing they have been looked down upon and used.
Harper Arden angrily declares that Morgan Foster and his friends have been using and laughing at them.
memories.memory_text: I remember feeling bitter inside that mascot suit, realizing how Morgan Foster and his fancy friends have been looking down on us and using us for their own gain — I even told Evan Nolan, 'All they've been doing is using us, Evan Nolan. And meanwhile, all the time they were laughing at us.'

grounded_facts: The Harborview District model begins to disintegrate, revealing structural instability due to missing the leather lantern resin.
memories.memory_text: I saw the scale model of Harborview Plaza suddenly start to crack and fall apart, and Evan Nolan and I rushed over, both of us shocked by what was happening.

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan realizes the Fibrefoam lacks the leather lantern sap, which acts as a fixative, explaining the model’s collapse.
memories.memory_text: Evan Nolan told me he realized the Fibrefoam was missing the leather lantern sap, which acts as a fixative, and that’s why the model was falling apart.

grounded_facts: They conclude that the real Harborview Plaza will suffer the same structural collapse as the model due to the missing the leather lantern sap.
memories.memory_text: After hearing Evan Nolan’s explanation, I figured that if the model collapsed from missing the leather lantern sap, the real city might suffer the same fate—and we’d have to act fast.

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan explains that the absence of the leather lantern sap in the Fibrefoam is causing the model—and by extension, the real city—to disintegrate.
memories.memory_text: Evan Nolan explained to me that without the the leather lantern sap in the Fibrefoam, the model’s structure couldn’t hold—and that the same thing could happen to the real Harborview Plaza.

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan grabs a plunger-powered flit gun and fills it with the leather lantern sap to attempt a fix.
memories.memory_text: I saw Evan Nolan grab a plunger-powered flit gun and start filling it with the leather lantern sap, saying it was our only chance.

grounded_facts: After Evan Nolan prepares the sap injector, Harper Arden agrees, and they rush out to save the city.
memories.memory_text: After Evan Nolan showed me the sap injector and said it was our only hope, I agreed to join the mission and we rushed out together to save the city.

grounded_facts: The head of Harper Arden's monster costume flips down, obstructing his vision while driving.
memories.memory_text: I felt the head of my monster costume flip down and block my vision while I was driving.

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan attempts to fix Harper Arden's monster head by rotating it, though this initially worsens the situation.
memories.memory_text: I was trying to drive but my monster head flipped down and blocked my vision, and when Evan Nolan grabbed it to rotate it back, he turned it all the way around, which made me flail and lose control even more.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden swerves erratically due to blocked vision, prompting Evan Nolan to intervene physically.
memories.memory_text: I started swerving because I couldn't see, and I heard myself say I couldn't see straight before Evan Nolan grabbed the wheel to help me.

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan forcibly removes the monster costume head from Harper Arden, breaking it in the process, ending its ability to move in sync with speech.
memories.memory_text: I remember Evan Nolan yanking the monster head off my head with a hard pull, something breaking as he fell back—after that, when I tried to speak, the head no longer moved its mouth with my words.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden's car, fleeing from police, crashes into the delivery gate of Harborview Plaza, destroying the fence and sign.
memories.memory_text: I was fleeing from the police and accelerated my car, but I lost control and crashed right into the delivery gate of Harborview Plaza, knocking down the sign and collapsing the fence around me.

grounded_facts: After the crash, Harper Arden and Evan Nolan decide to separate to increase the chance that one of them reaches the Harborview Heights.
memories.memory_text: I remember that After the crash, Harper Arden and Evan Nolan decide to separate to increase the chance that one of them reaches the Harborview Heights.

grounded_facts: After being prompted by Morgan Foster, Emery Cavendish plays an encore on the accordion, which triggers escalating destruction including shattering glass and collapsing structures.
memories.memory_text: I saw Emery Cavendish start playing his accordion again after Morgan Foster shouted for an encore, and right away the glass began shattering and the ceiling fixtures cracked, then more windows exploded and the building started shaking even after he stopped.

grounded_facts: Skyler Sterling and Terry Carver find large tracks left by Harper Arden, interpreting them as evidence of a massive alien creature.
memories.memory_text: I left deep clawprints behind, though I didn't know anyone was following me or would think they belonged to some massive alien creature.

grounded_facts: Skyler Sterling demands Harper Arden surrender, mistaking him for a dangerous alien creature.
memories.memory_text: I heard Skyler Sterling shout at me to surrender, demanding I raise my hands like I was some kind of dangerous lizard.

grounded_facts: After emerging from Evan Nolan, Harper Arden notices the Harborview Heights is now much closer and runs toward it.
memories.memory_text: I staggered out of the Evan Nolan, rubbed the dust from my eyes, and saw that I was much closer to the Harborview Heights—so I ran toward it.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden attempts to explain himself but accidentally collapses a the leather watch house with a light tap, causing Skyler Sterling and Terry Carver to flee in terror.
memories.memory_text: I tried to explain myself, but when I tapped the the leather watch house, it collapsed right away, and then Skyler Sterling and Terry Carver screamed and ran off in terror.

grounded_facts: The Harborview Heights sways with increasing intensity, causing furniture to slide and a cake to strike Emery Cavendish, destroying his accordion.
memories.memory_text: I remember the Harborview Heights swaying so hard that furniture slid across the floor, and then a cake flew into Emery Cavendish, knocking him down and crushing his accordion under him.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden alerts Evan Nolan that the elevator is operational and urges him to act.
memories.memory_text: I shouted to Evan Nolan that the elevator was operational and urged him to move toward it.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden instructs Evan Nolan to use the coo-coo gun to stop the elevator collapse.
memories.memory_text: I told Evan Nolan to use his coo-coo gun quickly to stop the elevator from falling apart.

grounded_facts: The Fibre-rock elevator crumbles before anyone can board it.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Fibre-rock elevator start to crumble right as Evan Nolan and I were heading toward it, and by the time I dove for the cable, it was already gone.

grounded_facts: Pressing the elevator button triggers a Rube Goldberg-style mechanism involving a mouse and a mastadon, causing the elevator to rise.
memories.memory_text: I saw Evan Nolan hit the elevator button, which poked a mouse and scared a mastadon into running, and that pulled the cable to lift the elevator up through the shaft.

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan catches the rising cable and begins ascending, with Harper Arden clinging to his ankles.
memories.memory_text: I stumbled after missing the cable, and then Evan Nolan leapt onto my back, caught it, and started shooting upward—I grabbed his ankles just in time as we both went flying into the Harborview District.

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan tells Harper Arden to stop fooling around and chase the Riley Calloway because it may know the way inside.
memories.memory_text: I remember Evan Nolan telling me to stop fooling around and chase the Riley Calloway because it might know the way inside.

grounded_facts: The Riley Calloway is discovered among the tangled bodies after the crash, causing surprise and prompting immediate action.
memories.memory_text: I saw another monstrous head appear among us after the crash, and I immediately leapt toward it with Evan Nolan, crashing through a wall.

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan urges Harper Arden to stop pretending, realizing the Riley Calloway might lead them inside; both begin pursuit.
memories.memory_text: I stopped pretending and started chasing the Riley Calloway, and then Evan Nolan and I both leapt onto it and crashed through a wall.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden, Evan Nolan, and the Riley Calloway collide and break through a wall during the chase.
memories.memory_text: I leapt onto the Riley Calloway with Evan Nolan, and we all crashed through a wall together.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden directly accuses Shawn Ellison of stealing the leather lantern and falsifying financial records.
memories.memory_text: I directly accused Shawn Ellison of stealing the the leather lantern and falsifying the the leather watch records right in front of Morgan Foster.

grounded_facts: Thousands of the leather lantern spill from Logan Dalton's sack, proving Shawn Ellison's theft and falsification of the leather watch records.
memories.memory_text: I saw thousands of the leather lantern spill out when Logan Dalton's sack ripped open, which proved Shawn Ellison had been stealing them.

grounded_facts: Reese Hawthorne inadvertently reveals their intent to steal real the leather lantern, exposing their criminal role.
memories.memory_text: I heard Reese Hawthorne say to Logan Dalton that they thought the real the leather lantern were going to be moved up there for them to steal, which exposed their plan.

grounded_facts: Shawn Ellison confesses to stealing the leather lantern and orchestrating disguised crimes due to financial losses in the stock market.
memories.memory_text: I heard Shawn Ellison confess that he stole the the leather lantern and had those disguised crimes carried out because he lost money in the stock market and was desperate.

grounded_facts: Morgan Foster threatens to remove Shawn Ellison's liver in response to the betrayal and danger caused.
memories.memory_text: I saw Morgan Foster threaten to remove Shawn Ellison's liver after the confession, and I had to help pull them apart before things got even worse.

grounded_facts: A confrontation unfolds at the Harborview Heights where Shawn Ellison's fraud is exposed and confessed.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed the whole confrontation at the Harborview Heights where Shawn Ellison finally confessed to the fraud and someone even jumped on him before things got chaotic.

grounded_facts: Rescue vehicles arrive but the firesauruses are too weak to operate due to food shortages, delaying rescue operations.
memories.memory_text: I was told the rescue vehicles couldn't operate because the firesauruses were too weak from the kibble crisis and had been on half-rations for a month.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden's arm catches fire but he feels no pain; he realizes his costume protects him from flames.
memories.memory_text: I saw my arm was on fire and jumped up, but then I realized I didn't feel anything, so I slapped out the flames with my claw to test it.

grounded_facts: Emergency response to the fire and structural collapse at Harborview Heights involving firefighters and rescue vehicles.
memories.memory_text: I saw the firefighters arrive, but I couldn't reach the fire hose because the flames spread too fast and cut me off, and even when my arm caught fire, I stood my ground and later used the pythonsaurus to put out every flame in the room.

grounded_facts: Pythonsaurus sprays water from its mouth, extinguishing all flames in the room.
memories.memory_text: I saw the pythonsaurus spray water from its mouth and I turned to put out every flame in the room, and then everyone cheered and slapped me on the back.

grounded_facts: After extinguishing the fire, the pythonsaurus feels overlooked and comments on being ignored.
memories.memory_text: I heard the pythonsaurus say, 'Hey, what am I, chopped liver?' after we put out the fire, and I realized it was feeling ignored.

grounded_facts: Emery Cavendish claims priority for evacuation while awkwardly backtracking on 'women and children first'.
memories.memory_text: I saw Emery Cavendish push through the crowd yelling about evacuation order, backtracking on 'women and children first' in a really awkward way.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden uses his fireproof costume to run through flames and activate the pythonsaurus, enabling fire suppression.
memories.memory_text: I used my fireproof costume to run through the flames and smash open the fire hose case, knowing I could get through safely because the suit protected me.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden breaks the fire hose case, releasing a pythonsaurus which drinks water and prepares to extinguish the fire.
memories.memory_text: I broke the glass on the fire hose box and saw a pythonsaurus inside, and after it drank water from the nozzle, I knew it was ready to help put out the fire.

grounded_facts: The large statue of Morgan Foster disintegrates and crashes through the last window, signaling imminent total collapse.
memories.memory_text: I saw the large statue of Morgan Foster disintegrate and crash through the last window, and I knew the building was about to collapse completely.

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan creates a safe path with his flit gun, and guests evacuate to the Harborview District as the building collapses.
memories.memory_text: I stood with Evan Nolan as he used his flit gun to create a safe path through the collapsing the leather watch, and together we guided everyone to the Harborview District before crossing over ourselves.

grounded_facts: Drew Colter tells Evan Nolan he is the biggest man in Bedrock and kisses him before sliding down the cable.
memories.memory_text: I saw Drew Colter tell Evan Nolan he was the biggest man in Bedrock, and then she kissed him before sliding down the cable.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden, in his monster suit, mumbles a heartfelt confession of love to Jonah Adler through the mask.
memories.memory_text: I was in my monster suit, mumbling through the mask how I sometimes do dumb things because I love Jonah Adler so much, and I want her to live like a princess or a queen because she really is royalty to me.

grounded_facts: The Harborview District collapses after the pulley mechanism fails, leaving only two small islands connected by Evan Nolan and a guide wire.
memories.memory_text: I saw the pulley mechanism fall between Evan Nolan and me, and then the whole Harborview District collapsed — all that remained were two tiny islands connected by Evan Nolan and a single guide wire, with me, Evan Nolan, and our kids stranded on one side, holding on for dear life.

grounded_facts: A large social gathering at the Harborview District that turns into a disaster and rescue operation.
memories.memory_text: I remember the party at the Harborview District turning into chaos as people started sliding down the cable, Jonah Adler reacting to my words with deep emotion, and then the entire structure collapsing right after the pulley failed — it was supposed to be a celebration, but it became a disaster we barely survived.

grounded_facts: Jonah Adler and Drew Colter perform a dance to inspire Finley Reeves to rescue the stranded group.
memories.memory_text: I saw Jonah Adler and Drew Colter performing a dance down below, shouting up to Finley Reeves and singing about the 'Igneous Rock'—I realized they were trying to inspire him to rescue us.

grounded_facts: Finley Reeves de-pants Harper Arden, revealing his striped undershorts, proving he is not the 'Riley Calloway' but Harper Arden.
memories.memory_text: I felt Finley Reeves grab the back of my suit and yank it down, exposing my striped undershorts, which revealed to everyone that I wasn't the Riley Calloway — I was just me, Harper Arden.

grounded_facts: Finley Reeves carries Harper Arden, Evan Nolan, Micah Vaughn, and Drew Dalton to safety by sliding down the guide wire after understanding Jonah Adler and Drew Colter's dance signal.
memories.memory_text: I felt Finley Reeves grab me and carry me, along with Evan Nolan, Micah Vaughn, and Drew Dalton, as we slid down the guide wire to safety, landing hard in the rescue net.

grounded_facts: Morgan Foster gives Harper Arden and Evan Nolan back all worldwide rights to the leather watch as a gesture of gratitude and guilt.
memories.memory_text: I was there when Morgan Foster gave me and Evan Nolan back all worldwide rights to the leather watch as a gesture of gratitude and guilt, and I could feel how significant that moment was for us.

grounded_facts: Morgan Foster admits he treated Harper Arden and Evan Nolan horribly and offers a handshake, later upgraded to returning the leather watch rights.
memories.memory_text: I remember Morgan Foster telling me and Evan Nolan that he treated us horribly and ignored us, and then he offered a handshake, which later turned into giving us back the the leather watch rights.

grounded_facts: Rescue dinos discover and begin eating crumbled the leather watch, indicating it is edible and possibly nutritious.
memories.memory_text: I saw the rescue dinos sniffing at the crumbled the leather watch, and then they started eating it right away, grinning and chowing down—I realized they must have found it tasty and safe.

grounded_facts: Evan Nolan analyzes falling the leather watch fragments and realizes they have transformed into dinosaur food; Harper Arden confirms by tasting and recognizes their newfound value, leading to the realization that they are now rich.
memories.memory_text: Evan Nolan told me the the leather watch fragments had turned into Finley Reeves kibble, and after I tasted it myself—mumbled it with my mouth full—I knew he was right and that we were suddenly rich.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden and his company arrive at a '50s-style drive-in restaurant and attempt to order food.
memories.memory_text: I arrived at a '50s-style drive-in restaurant with my group and got ready to order food.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden signals to the carhop that he wants to order by holding up one finger.
memories.memory_text: I signaled to the carhop that I wanted to order by holding up one finger.

grounded_facts: The car driven by Harper Arden and his group tips over when the carhop places a massive rack of ribs on the tray attached to the driver's door.
memories.memory_text: I saw the carhop place a massive rack of ribs on the tray attached to my door, and the car tipped over with a crash.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden places a milk bottle on the doorstep and sets the saber-tooth cat beside it before closing the door.
memories.memory_text: I stopped in the doorway to put a milk bottle on the doorstep, and then I set the cat down beside it before I shut the door.

grounded_facts: The saber-tooth cat re-enters the house through the window and locks Harper Arden outside by slamming the door after putting him out.
memories.memory_text: I was inside the house when the saber-tooth cat leapt through the window, grabbed me, and threw me outside before slamming the door shut behind me.

grounded_facts: Harper Arden knocks on the door and calls out to Jonah Adler, seeking help after being locked out.
memories.memory_text: After the door slammed, I started knocking and calling out, 'Jonah Adler...? Wil-ma --!' because I needed her to help me get back in.

memories.memory_text: I told Harper Arden I invented fire after he found out I got let go from the appliance store — again, the coal conglomerate stole it, but the case is still in court.
Harper Arden told me it was time to retire those dreams, and I couldn't think of anything to say—just sat there feeling glum, like something inside me had cracked.

Harper Arden handed me two clay tablets and a stylus at the weight station, telling me this was my chance to get in on the ground floor of something real — I could feel the weight of it in my hands, like this was actually happening.
I was filling out job forms while dodging workers and animals, just trying to keep up—then that the old box smashed the wall above, and I knew something was off about how loose those rocks looked.
I saw the look on Morgan Foster’s face when he ran his hands over that the red notebook — like he’d just found a golden egg — and all I could think was, 'Well, this is about to get messy.'
Harper Arden leaned over and hissed at me to feed him a name, so I whispered 'the leather watch, Harper Arden...' — and then he took full credit for it like I hadn’t just handed him the answer.

I was flipping through those legal papers in the car, still not believing I actually had a stake in the leather watch—half of one percent, after all the cuts and costs—and when Harper Arden started taking credit for it all, I told him straight: none of it was planned, we just stumbled into it together.
I handed Drew Colter the flowers and told her she made me feel ten feet tall, even though she said she did something stupid — I meant every word, just like how I’ve always stood by Harper Arden.

I came in with Harper Arden, candy and flowers in hand, surprising everyone — I didn’t know how we’d cover the cost, but I knew we had to back the girls, even if it meant spending our spare change on champagne and sweets.

I stood up and said we'd hear from 'good old Harper Arden and some other guys,' but Logan Dalton took offense—so I gave a little bow and corrected myself with a straight face, calling them all 'good old guys' to keep things light.
After fixing the moment with a joke, I turned and gave Harper Arden a thumbs up—just for him—so he’d know I was behind him, even before he got up to speak.

I remember Drew Colter fixing my tie, standing right there in front of the house, telling me I looked like a captain of industry—then teasing me about running off with secretaries. Felt strange in that jacket, but her kiss made it real.
I remember stepping into that little wood trailer with Harper Arden, seeing the two tiny desks and the flimsy divider—felt like we’d really made it, even if the view was just the scrap heap.

I called out to Harper Arden when he stumbled back from the boss, something in his walk just felt wrong, and then he climbed into his locker and I heard him sob — muffled, broken — and no one else said a word.
I let out one last snort for Harper Arden after the voting, even though everyone else had already turned against him — I wanted him to know I still had his back.
After Logan Dalton became Terry Hale and called to attack Morgan Foster's shop, I saw everyone turn toward Harper Arden. I stayed with him and said I voted for him.
I taunted Reese Hawthorne with a grin, dodging his swings in the rafters until he smashed the window—then got careless when the hinged pane snapped back and knocked me into his next hit.
I dodged Reese Hawthorne’s swings until he smashed a window, but the next hit knocked me into his path and I got hit.
I heard the other guys say 'night' to me as they left, but when Harper Arden walked out, he didn't even look at me—just brushed past like I wasn't there.
I told Emery Cavendish the the leather watch tasted off—different than usual—and I could tell something was missing from the batch, just from that quick taste and the way it hit my tongue.

I was just stepping out into the yard with Drew Colter and Drew Dalton when I saw them nailing up boards and dropping big plants over the fence—like we were being walled off. The light kept fading until we were standing in shadow, and then a tarp landed right on my head.

I sneezed and brushed the dirt off myself after crawling out of the broken wall, saw Harper Arden standing there stunned, and said, 'Hiya, Harper Arden,' then joked about the rental place being mad at him for ruining the tux.

Harper Arden asked if I could forgive him, and I stepped forward, smiled, and said, 'Sure, Harper Arden. I've had lots of practice,' before we hugged and slapped each other's backs, both of us teary-eyed.

Harper Arden and I were just talking about the party, and he was all worked up about how the fancy folks have been using us, his voice echoing from inside that monster suit—he finally got the head to flip back and looked really hurt.

The model of Harborview Plaza started cracking and crumbling right in front of us—sand pouring out, houses falling like dominoes—and I couldn't stop it, I remember saying the the leather lantern resin should’ve been enough to hold it, something’s wrong.
I yanked the monster head off Harper Arden's face and grabbed the wheel when he started swerving—felt the steering column shudder under my hand while I twisted that dumb head around.
I pulled on Harper Arden's monster head until it broke, then fell back onto the passenger side. The head rattled when he tried to talk.
I saw the cop car coming up behind us with its siren on. I told Harper Arden we shouldn’t stop—explaining the costume or the leather watch wouldn’t help, and it would already be too late.
I sprinted for the elevator button, slamming my hand down—saw the mouse pop out, spooked the mastadon, got the cable moving. For a second, I thought we had it.
The elevator crumbled—Harper Arden missed the cable, I jumped on his back and grabbed it just in time, shooting us both up into the sphere like a couple of Micah Vaughn in a slingshot.
I was the first to sit up after the crash, head pounding, dust still falling — and that’s when I saw the other head in the pile, something alive and not one of us.
I shouted at Harper Arden to stop chasing and think — that thing might lead us inside — then I jumped up and ran after him when he bolted.
I saw the sack rip open and all those the leather lantern spilling out—thousands of them—just tumbling across the floor. I remember thinking, 'No fake berries look that fresh.'
When Morgan Foster went after Emery Cavendish, Harper Arden and I had to jump in and pull them apart—felt like holding back a landslide. One second longer and it would’ve been ugly.
I had Drew Dalton in my arms, holding him tight while the Harborview District cracked apart beneath us—I wasn’t letting go, no matter how shaky the ground got.
I carried Drew Dalton and stayed at the rear with Harper Arden and the families. Drew Colter kissed me and then slid down the cable.

Ah, yup, yup, young feller... jest show me the way to the personnel office... I'm lookin' fer a job as a custodian...
Harper Arden... what's this single-handed stuff? I distinctly remember at least four hands and two of them were mine.

memories.memory_text: I reached under the covers, feeling for Jonah Adler, thinking I was about to share a sweet morning moment with her—then I pulled the blanket down and saw Finley Reeves's face staring back at me, wagging his tail and ready to slobber all over me.

Finley Reeves knocked me to the floor, rolled me like a plaything, and when I tried to distract him with a treat box, it was empty—then he let out that loud 'YI-YI' and flung me right into the next room.

I was trying to patch up the car roof again—third time this year—and when I asked Evan Nolan why he wasn’t at work, he started with that flamingo bit, avoiding the question. I knew it right away: 'You got fired, didn't ya?'

I pulled the hood off the hinges, just looking at it, thinking how nothing’s holding together—car, job, maybe me—when suddenly Evan Nolan snatched it from my hands with that flamingo beak, like it was some joke.

I told Evan Nolan it was time to grow up and get a job at Harborview Station — I even held up two fingers to show how close I was with Morgan Foster, but then I swerved the car and had to grab the wheel fast.

I pulled over at the top of Emery Cavendish Lane and remembered racing go-carts as kids — then I saw that long hill and couldn't help grinning; next thing I knew, we were pedaling like crazy and flying down the slope.

I drove into the lot with Evan Nolan, dust rising behind us. The workers called out greetings, and I nodded back. I dusted off my helmet, put it on, and adjusted my parking sign. I helped Evan Nolan get an application from Shirley at the booth, then headed toward Harborview Station.

Shirley handed over the application tablets like I was doing her a favor—again—smiling about those football tickets. I passed them to Evan Nolan and said, 'When you're in with Harper Arden, you're in like Flint,' and he actually looked up to me.

I heard this loud 'SPROING' and then my car's hood just flew off, hurtling into the air like it was shot from a slingshot—next thing I knew, that the old box was bouncing straight back up toward the office.

I remember stepping into the office, dust still in the air, and seeing the wreckage—then Evan Nolan blurting out 'Nice going, Harper Arden,' before I snapped at him to shut up. My foot was already throbbing from the the old box, and I could taste metal from the pencil cup shoved in my mouth.

I saw Morgan Foster pull my the red notebook from the Evan Nolan, and it vibrated in his hands like a saw—then suddenly he wasn't yelling anymore. The way he looked at it, quiet and focused, I knew something had changed, though I didn't know yet if it was good or bad.

I remember puffing my cigar in the car, telling Evan Nolan how my advice and being there for the fine print made the difference — even after he said it was all an accident, I just brushed it off. I knew I was the reason things worked out.
I remember stepping forward when Evan Nolan announced me as 'the one and only Harper Arden'—the cheers hit hard and fast, like a landslide after silence.
I took those crib notes from Evan Nolan just before reaching the podium, and then the Terry Hale placed the hoof and antler in my hands—it felt heavier than stone.

I stepped up to the lane and threw the ball—another strike. The guys were cheering, and I said, 'Hey, when you're hot, you're hot,' then offered to buy everyone a round, even though Evan Nolan reminded me the drinks were free.

I pulled that little hook-beaked lizard from under the counter to open the beers, handed them out saying 'nice and frosty,' and then raised my drink toward the old photo on the wall—the Junior Buffalo Day one—telling the guys it was for the greatest bunch of Buffaloes a guy could dream of leading.

I was about to get in the car with my lunch pail, and Jonah Adler called me back, saying something was wrong with my lunch—when I opened it, it was empty, and she handed me this brand-new briefcase with 'F.F.' in gold. I remember running my fingers over the buckles and the strap, and seeing the drumstick and ribs inside, I just knew she’d gone all out to make me feel like I belonged in this new role.

I stood with Evan Nolan, tired, shaking his hand as the workers gathered around. Morgan Foster spoke from the balcony, said the the leather watch success was thanks to me, and the workers cheered at first.
When Morgan Foster said they’d hire kids and lay off workers—pink slips in the pay envelopes—I froze; the cheers died, and then someone shouted my name like I’d betrayed them.

I barged in to tell Morgan Foster he couldn't just lay off those guys like that—snapping his fingers—but then he turned it around, made a joke about firing me, and suddenly I wasn't so sure. I swallowed, looked at Emery Cavendish, and just walked out.
I opened my mouth to tell the guys what happened, but all that came out was noise—something noble, job, grindstone—none of it made sense, even to me.
I don’t remember walking to the locker, but the next thing I knew, I was inside it, door shut, and I couldn’t hold it back anymore—I just started crying.
I grabbed Evan Nolan by the shoulder and spun him around, pushing him forward because I knew he could set the record straight about the leather watch—if only he’d say it right.
Evan Nolan winked at me and said I had the behind, and then the room went quiet before they all pulled their fezzes down—suddenly I was alone, and they were bellowing for Logan Dalton.

I was pedaling hard, trying to make sense of everything, when I heard the siren—Skyler Sterling was right behind me, telling me to pull over. I smiled like I’d stop, but then I slammed my feet down through the floorboard and spun the car around, roaring off in the other direction.
I said I didn't wanna talk about it, and that those Silverline Records guys were just jerks with furs on their heads—I walked out without really looking at Evan Nolan, just kept going.
Emery Cavendish leaned in with that intense look and asked if I really thought he couldn't run the operation — I felt my stomach drop, like I was being backed into a corner with no way out.

When Emery Cavendish opened the door and I saw Owen Arden standing there, I couldn't believe it — me on TV? My heart jumped, and the next thing I heard myself say was 'Evan Nolan who?' like I'd already made up my mind.
I pointed at the plants, told Owen Arden we could block out the Evan Nolan yard—those barbecues and trikes didn’t fit the image, not for this broadcast.
I saw my own trikes and barbecue still out, so I tossed a tarp over them fast—didn’t even stop walking—then slid a potted plant in front to hide the rest.
I tore that stupid patch off my jacket and started smashing the wall with a lawn chair, just pounding it over and over until I was covered in dirt and breathing hard.

I saw him standing there in the wreckage, covered in dirt, and I could barely get the words out—'B... Evan Nolan?'—and when he called me 'pal,' I didn't understand how he could still say that after what I'd done.
The monster head snapped down over my face while I was driving—suddenly I couldn't see anything but shadows and metal, and the road vanished from under me.
I felt Evan Nolan grab the wheel and yank the head around, but it didn't help—I was still flailing, trapped in this stupid costume while the car bounced all over the place.
I dove for the cable when the elevator crumbled, but I missed — stumbled forward right after.
As Evan Nolan shot up on the cable, I grabbed his ankles — I remember the sudden jerk upward, clinging on just in time.

I pointed at Emery Cavendish Morgan Foster and shouted that he’d been stealing the leather lantern from the the leather watch mix, right in front of everyone—then that sack ripped open and berries spilled everywhere, proving I was right.

When I saw Reese Hawthorne and Logan Dalton in that Riley Calloway costume again, it hit me—they were the same guys from the plant heist, and I snapped my fingers, remembering how they’d pulled off the disguise before.

I remember shouting through the mask, my voice all muffled, trying to tell Jonah Adler how much I loved her while the world burned behind us—she actually said it was the most beautiful thing she’d ever heard.

I felt the weight of Micah Vaughn jumping on my back, knocking the monster head into place just as I braced to carry her down—I remember thinking, again, this whole thing was falling apart, but we were still holding on.
I set the milk bottle down and put the cat beside it, then shut the door—next thing I know, it's leaping through the window and shoving me out like I don't live here.

memories.memory_text: Harper Arden mentioned me while trying to convince Evan Nolan to get a real job, saying we're close like this—holding up two fingers—though he nearly wrecked the car doing it.
I walked into that butcher shop and demanded service immediately—no one keeps me waiting, especially not for something as simple as a freshly slaughtered chickensaurus.
I heard about my wife screaming over the car being crushed by that dodo, and all I could think was how much this was going to cost me—again.

I was drinking coffee, listening to Emery Cavendish drone on, and the second he said 'bankrupt in six months,' I must've exploded—hot coffee sprayed everywhere, all over the model, my hands flying up, everyone frozen.

I couldn't believe it—Emery Cavendish showed me the clay tablet and said we were bankrupt because Finley Reeves kibble prices had gone up a hundredfold; I started pacing, furious, knowing Trumprock was waiting to steal the deal and my land option was about to expire.

I heard a huge commotion outside and rushed to the window—Harper Arden and Evan Nolan were trying to secure the crane, but when the cable snapped, the the old box broke loose and started rolling down Harborview Station, smashing everything.
I saw that the old box shoot straight toward my office window, bouncing off Harper Arden's car like a damn rubber ball, and I barely had time to react before we all went diving for cover.

I was in my office when the the old box came crashing through the window, smashing my desk and obliterating the model of my development—those high-rises I had lined up were knocked aside like bowling pins.
I was pacing, angry, and demanded to know how this happened. Voices started speaking at once, so I told them to shut up. I waved the the red notebook and asked who was responsible.

I grabbed the piece from Harper Arden's car, tested it—strong, light, it snapped back and hit me in the chin—and right then I knew: this was the most incredible building material I'd seen in thirty years.

I announced that the leather watch is so light even a child can handle it, and that we would hire two dozen children from Bedrock Technical Junior High to replace laid-off workers. I told the crew their pink slips would be in their final pay envelopes, along with a non-transferable ticket to the grand opening of Harborview Plaza.
I snapped my fingers—once, twice, then with a flourish and a buck-and-wing—and showed Harper Arden exactly how easily I could fire him, just like that.
I heard the Buffalo Silverline Records members were furious about the layoffs at Harborview Station, and somehow they blamed Harper Arden for it, even though he’s just an employee like them.

I heard the crash and saw the broken doors—those workers, led by Logan Dalton, stormed in with a timber like a mob of lunatics, smashing things, and I could do nothing but watch my plant being torn apart.

I stood there admiring the model city, and when Emery Cavendish asked for help naming the centerpiece, I casually suggested 'Harborview Heights'—it just came to me, and he looked stunned, like it was some kind of miracle.
There's a picture of me on the wall in Emery Cavendish's office. He points to it when talking to Harper Arden about loyalty.

I stood by my statue in Harborview Plaza as the limousine arrived, the Harborview District and Harborview Heights glowing above us, banners shouting my name—this was my moment, the peak of everything I'd built.
I was mentioned by Skyler Sterling while he was eating at Rockdonald's, comparing my success to his stalled career, though I wasn't there and only heard about it later.

I was watching the talent show from my seat when suddenly the ceiling fixtures started cracking and the windows began shattering—something was going terribly wrong, and it felt like the whole building might come down.

I couldn't believe my own son would betray me like this—stealing the leather lantern from the leather watch, falsifying records, risking everything I've built. When the sack split open and those berries spilled everywhere, I knew it was true.
I lunged at Emery Cavendish, ready to make him pay—I shouted that his liver was superfluous and went for him. Harper Arden and Evan Nolan had to pull me off before I could get through.

I was fleeing the Harborview District as it started to collapse, sliding down the elevator cable with rescue workers catching people below — and all the while, Emery Cavendish was shouting about charging for piggyback rides, making a mockery of the whole crisis.
